title: XNet v2: Fewer Limitations, Better Results and Greater Universality
mechanism: A Haar wavelet split gives low- and high-frequency images, remixed with random weights (x_L = I_L + a I_H, x_H = I_H + b I_L). Three sub-networks (raw, LF, HF) are trained with consistency and feature-level LF/HF fusion.
adaptation: 1-channel Haar of the 512 px cell. HF carries cracks and fingers, LF carries inactive and dark regions. Two uses: (a) supervised XNet v2 as a benchmark arm; (b) the random LF/HF remix as a label-safe augmentation on U-Net++.
min_experiment: Arm: house + LF/HF remix augmentation (a, b in [0, 0.5]), 5-fold CV. Baseline: house. Metric: inactive IoU, BMRK crack IoU. Kill: no gain larger than 1 SE on CV. Separately run official XNet v2 supervised as a benchmark entry.
evidence: R with full supervision: CREMI Jaccard 75.47 (UNet) -> 79.80, GlaS 81.54 -> 84.03, ISIC-2017 74.49 -> 76.04. XNet (ICCV 2023) repo verified at github.com/Yanfeng-Zhou/XNet.
prior_overlap: Pseudo-label SSL at 100% was n.d., but XNet's frequency-split consistency and LF/HF remix augmentation were never run.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark arm on 1-channel 512 px; for our model, use the random LF/HF remix as a label-safe augmentation on U-Net++ (HF carries cracks and fingers, LF carries inactive).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark run of supervised XNet v2 (about 10 GPU-h); separate arm house + LF/HF remix vs house, kill if CV gain below 1 SE on inactive and BMRK crack IoU.
